Key: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f=S·(t−1)/t where S=n−1 and t=smallest divisor ≥3 of S (t∤3⇒t|c).  
For c=0,4M: t=4 ⇒ g=3/4−1/A, 15/4−1/A.  
For small c>0: g=1−⌈A/t⌉/A with t=11,5081287,4,17.  
A=2025!.  
Sum ⇒ p/q=6059/748−(Q+3)/A, Q=⌊A/5081287⌋.  
p+q≡6807·(A·748⁻¹)−Q−3 (mod 99991).  
Compute A mod 99991=57239, inv748=43980, inv5081287≡84352, A mod 5081287=66034 ⇒ Q≡57380.  
Result =93086. Pitfall: sign of ε (c−M) changes floor.

Use f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f=S·(t−1)/t where S=n−1 and t=smallest divisor ≥3 of S (t∤3). For M=3^N, S≈M+k ⇒ t=smallest divisor of k+1 not 2. Compute t: c=0→4, 4M→4, 1848374→11, 10162574→5081287, 265710644→4, 44636594→17. g(c)=1−⌈2025!/t⌉/2025! (c>0) and g(0)=3/4−1/2025!. Sum → p/q=6059/748−(⌈A/5081287⌉+2)/A, A=2025!. Compute A mod 99991, A/748 mod 99991, Q=⌊A/5081287⌋ mod 99991. Result p+q≡93086 (mod 99991). Pitfalls: ensure t≠2, handle c=0 sign, use ceil for non‑divisible t.

We need f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Set a=1; then n−1=S must have a proper divisor t≥3. Minimal LCM=S−S/t, where t is smallest proper divisor of S (t≠2). For each case compute S=M+c−1. Since M=3^{2025!}, for any t≤2025, t∤3 ⇒ M≡1 (mod t). Thus S≡c (mod t). So t is smallest divisor ≥3 of c (excluding 2) unless c−1 divisible by 3 (none here). Hence:
c=0 → t=4; c=4M → t=4; c=1848374 → t=11; c=10162574 → t=5081287 (prime); c=265710644 → t=4; c=44636594 → t=17.
Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(M+c)/M⌋/2025! = (t−1)/t for t|A (A=2025!) else =1−⌈A/t⌉/A. Using A=2025!,
g(0)=3/4−1/A, g(4M)=15/4−1/A,
g(1848374)=10/11, g(265710644)=3/4, g(44636594)=16/17,
g(10162574)=1−⌈A/5081287⌉/A.
Sum = 6059/748 − (⌈A/5081287⌉+3)/A = (6807·A/748 −⌈A/5081287⌉−3)/A.
Compute A mod 99991, A/748 mod 99991, ⌈A/5081287⌉ mod 99991 via modular inverses:
A≡57239, A/748≡97795, ⌈A/5081287⌉≡Q+1 with Q≡57380 (mod 99991).
Thus p+q≡6807·97795−57380−3≡93086 (mod 99991).

Use f(N)= (N‑1)(p‑1)/p, p=smallest divisor>2 of N‑1. For N=M+c (M=3^{2025!}) compute p: c=0→4; c=4M→4; 1848374→11; 10162574→5081287; 265710644→4; 44636594→17.  
g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025! = (p‑1)/p, except subtract 1/2025! for c=0,4M and subtract r/(p·2025!) for p=5081287 (r=(2025! mod p)(p‑1) mod p).  
Sum S =21/4+10/11+5081286/5081287+16/17 –(2+ r/p)/2025!.  
Denominator D=p·2025!. Compute numerator N = p[21·(2025!/4)+10·(2025!/11)+16·(2025!/17)]+(p‑1)·2025! –(2p+r).  
Find N mod 99991, D mod 99991 (use factorial mod, inverses of 4,11,17).  
Result (N+D) mod 99991 = 55210.   (Pitfall: handle c=0,4M corrections; p may not divide 2025!.)

f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Ratio r=n⁻¹·lcm= p·q/(p·q+p+q) for a|c,b|c (p=c/a,q=c/b). Minimal r=6/11 (p,q=2,3) if 11|n; else 4/7 (p,q=2,4) if 7|n; else 10/17 (2,5) if 17|n; else larger. For M=3^K, K=2025!; M≡1 (mod p) for p≤K+1. S=M+c: divisors are primes of c+1 (≠3). Compute smallest divisor t≥6 of S; r= min_{(p,q)} p·q/(p·q+p+q) with t0=p·q+p+q|t. g(c)=⌊K·f(S)/M⌋/K = r (since K·r integer). Sum g’s = Σr_i. Compute r_i via smallest t|S_i giving best (p,q). Pitfalls: assume 1 divisor always used; need chain a|b|c; check S_i not divisible by 7,11,17 etc. Use factorization of c_i+1. Compute r_i for each c. Finally p+q mod 99991.

f(n)=S−S/t where S=n−1 and t=smallest divisor≥3 of S (proper). For M=3^{2025!}, S=M−1→t=4; S=5M−1→t=4; for c’s, t=11,5081287,4,17.  
g(c)=1−ceil(2025!/t)/2025! (c>0), g(0)=3/4−1/2025!, g(4M)=15/4−1/2025!.  
Sum ⇒ p+q≡6807·(2025!/748)−⌈2025!/5081287⌉−3 (mod 99991).  
Compute 2025! mod 99991=57239, inv748=43980, inv5081287=84352, get result 93086. Pitfall: ensure t|S (use proper divisor) and handle floor’s −1/A for c=0,4M.

f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N ⇒ N=L+L/p₁+L/p₂, L=S·p₁p₂/D, D=p₁p₂+p₁+p₂. For coprime p₁,p₂, D|S. Minimal L ⇒ smallest A=p₁p₂/D. Smallest A from p₁=2, D≡2(mod 3). For S=M+c (c≪M), D|c+1. Choose smallest divisor D≥11, D≡2 (mod 3). Then g(c)=2·((D−2)/3)/D=2/3−4/(3D). Cases: c=0,4M ⇒ D=27 ⇒ g=2/3. c=1848374⇒D=53⇒g=34/53. c=10162574⇒D=47⇒g=30/47. c=265710644⇒D=197⇒g=130/197. c=44636594⇒D=167⇒g=110/167. Sum=966630412/245854227 ⇒ (p+q) mod 99991 = 93764.

Key: f(n)=n·min_{s|n}h(s)/s, where h(s)=min LCM of 3 distinct ints sum s. For n=M+c (c≪M) divisors are s|t where t=(c+1)/3^{v₃(c+1)}. Compute min ratio h(s)/s over s|t. Brute h(s) for needed s (≤≈200) or use recursion; results: g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25, g(10162574)=30/47, g(265710644)=64/97, g(44636594)=110/167. Sum=125561848/19033825 → (p+q) mod 99991 = 8687. Pitfall: ensure s coprime to 3, use t’s divisors only.
